Everglades City is home to 352 people, where about 800 residents across three coastal settlements live surrounded by water. When Everglades National Park phased out commercial fishing in its waters, federal authorities sought to protect the mangrove wilderness and marine life of the Ten Thousand Islands. On the other side, commercial fishing families had worked these channels for generations, arguing that closing the water took away their livelihood while guided tour boats were still permitted to bring visitors across the boundary. An appeals court upheld the regulation, leaving local crabbers to work only the open Gulf outside the park line. When a park is created to protect natural waters, who should carry the cost of closing them: the local fishing families, or the broader public? Which side do you lean toward, and why? And tell us where you're watching from, and whether your community borders a protected park. 👇
